curriculum.lesson_evidence: To make a print, plan the design on paper first, then draw it lightly into the foam tile with a blunt pencil so the lines are pushed in. Roll a thin layer of paint evenly across the tile, place the paper on top, press with a clean hand or a clean roller, and peel it off slowly. Reprint by re-rolling the paint. Lay prints flat to dry and clean the tile and tools straight away. Press, don't slide, so the print does not smudge.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Your first print is patchy and some lines are missing. Name two changes you could make for the next print.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Roll the paint more evenly over the whole tile, and press with the flat of my hand all over so the paper touches every part.' Patchy prints come from uneven paint or uneven pressure.

WATCH FOR
Thinking that sliding the paper makes it stick better. Sliding blurs and smudges the print, so press down firmly without moving the paper.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Design and make a foam tile print with a simple picture of your choice, then print it at least four times. Make one in a second colour. Write one sentence about what the repeated prints look like together and what you would change.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teaching.model: To make a print, plan the design on paper first, then draw it lightly into the foam tile with a blunt pencil so the lines are pushed in. Roll a thin layer of paint evenly across the tile, place the paper on top, press with a clean hand or a clean roller, and peel it off slowly. Reprint by re-rolling the paint. Lay prints flat to dry and clean the tile and tools straight away. Press, don't slide, so the print does not smudge. Now choose a different subject or piece to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same arts idea in a new artwork, song, drama or dance, not a copy of the example. Review clarity, safety and respectful practice.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.
